title: Features only on open PR branches
summary:
This part decides which features that existed only on the nine draft PRs (#62 to #70) enter the rewrite, and in what form; #70 has since been merged into `main` as it is (2026-10-26, INT-52), and the other eight are still open. Daniel's FEA-BR-01 and FEA-BR-08 answers bring controls and tabs in, and his FEA-BR-08 note says PRs #62, #63, #65, #66, #67, #68 and #69 all enter the rewrite. Each card states the feature as the rewrite would build it; what the branch does, and where it falls short, sits under sources and conflicts. The branches themselves are part 08 (OPN-06 to OPN-14) and their formats part 05 (TYP-76 to TYP-81). Branch features another part already decides are not repeated: Daniel's #67 chart calls (one modal, labelled actions, PNG and SVG downloads, years as years, sparse labels, a lighter tooltip) are part 04a (FEA-CH-21, FEA-CH-28, FEA-CH-42 to FEA-CH-44, FEA-CH-46, FEA-CH-47), #69's navigation and docs gallery content are part 04c (FEA-SF-28, FEA-SF-43), and #67's style selector and measure key are recorded here only as pointers (FEA-BR-17, FEA-BR-18) to STY-05, STY-07, STY-08, STY-30, TYP-89 and FEA-SF-36.

The decisions that matter most:

- **Playable charts** (FEA-BR-01 to FEA-BR-07, FEA-BR-31 to FEA-BR-34, FEA-BR-36): whether authored controls enter the format, with the smooth transitions and fixed axes #62 lacks. Built and run, #62's controls work on the scatter but not on the line chart.
- **Multi-tab reports** (FEA-BR-08 to FEA-BR-10, FEA-BR-35, FEA-BR-38 to FEA-BR-40, FEA-BR-48): whether tabs enter the format, with every panel readable without the runtime, which the branch breaks.
- **Checks** (FEA-BR-20, FEA-BR-33, FEA-BR-37, FEA-BR-47): every reachable control state, browser suites for controls and tabs, and where #68's harness lands. They run per batch in the release run on `pre-prod`, not on every `dev` merge (DEL-81).
- **Site round** (FEA-BR-21, FEA-BR-22, FEA-BR-41): the bar the restored landing motion must clear, one docs page per chart type (answer with FEA-SF-43 and FEA-SF-46), and #65's sourced examples for those pages.
- **Famous charts** (FEA-BR-12): rendered, only Gapminder keeps the original's form.
- **RichView Publish** (FEA-BR-23 to FEA-BR-30, FEA-BR-44 to FEA-BR-46, FEA-BR-49): Daniel's INT-31 answer builds Publish in the rewrite, on a server core it shares with RichView Cowork, and makes RichView News one Publish instance; these cards are its requirements, and #70's code is evidence, not a base (INT-49). FEA-BR-30 reverses S27-655's dashboard pages.
- **Out, or Publish's secondary path** (FEA-BR-11, FEA-BR-14 to FEA-BR-16, FEA-BR-43): the voice dashboard stays a reference record (INT-34); data connectors are the secondary live-data path every RichView server offers (INT-24, OPN-63; the core never queries data, INT-08), recorded as the rules any engine must meet. FEA-BR-14 records that #66's SQL path can read files on the host.

Accepting some cards changes cards in other parts: TYP-77 gains `all` on filters (FEA-BR-03); TYP-16 gains a log scale (FEA-BR-12); FEA-RP-18 and TYP-34 follow FEA-BR-48 on `{#id}`; FEA-RP-10 gains per-panel notes (FEA-BR-40); FEA-CH-45 gains an exception for charts with controls (FEA-BR-32); TYP-79 gains MetricFlow's `group_by`, `where`, `order_by` and `limit` and SQL `params` (FEA-BR-15, FEA-BR-43); TYP-80 drops `dashboard` (FEA-BR-30); DEL-15 gains two suites and the worker-reply hold (FEA-BR-37, FEA-BR-47); FEA-SF-36's conflict about kept chart state no longer applies (FEA-BR-17).

How to answer: **accept** keeps the proposal as the rewrite's rule; **edit** replaces it with your text; **reject** drops the feature from the rewrite; **defer** leaves it open. Branch facts were read at each PR's head (#62 `a703897`, #63 `f1cb254`, #64 `81110e0`, #65 `850032b`, #66 `4ecef05`, #67 `47d8848`, #68 `bba45ab`, #69 `5e69843`, #70 `3f5c35f`) and are marked by confidence. On 2026-10-22 #62 and #63 were built and their examples run in headless Chromium, #65's pages were rendered with `main`'s build, and news.richview.ai and richview.ai were checked live; the #65-shell screenshot is that run's own capture, and #64's own captures stay local because they show business metrics from a demo dataset. Screenshots are in `screenshots/branches/`. Part 08's cross-part contradiction cards (OPN-50 to OPN-68) decide conflicts involving this part's cards and should be answered first.

items.title: Authored chart controls
items.question: Do authored chart controls from PR #62 (playback, filter, metric and variant) enter the rewrite's chart format?
items.why: Accepting adds `controls:` (TYP-77) and a stateful chart runtime to the first cut and makes FEA-BR-02 to FEA-BR-07, FEA-BR-31 to FEA-BR-34 and FEA-BR-36 binding. Rejecting keeps every chart one authored view, and the famous Gapminder chart stays a single year.
items.proposed: A chart block may carry `controls:`, an ordered list of dimensions a reader can change, of four kinds: `playback`, `filter`, `metric` and `variant`. The author declares every dimension and its options; readers cannot compose views of their own. Each state is resolved from the authored data alone, and every state at rest is a complete chart with exact values; readouts, labels, Table and CSV never show interpolated or invented observations. Controls are chart-local and never link two charts (INT-33). Without the runtime or WebGL, the chart shows ARC-05's fallback for its initial state, which is open (Daniel's INT-31 answer makes WebGL the default). The Gapminder-style scatter (playback and filter) and the indicator line (playback and metric) join the golden inputs (INT-55).

options.label: All four kinds
options.detail: What Daniel asked for on 2026-10-17; four schemas and a stateful runtime in the first cut.

options.label: Playback only
options.detail: Keeps the animated Gapminder story; filter, metric and variant wait until after launch.

options.label: Defer controls
options.detail: Smallest first cut; every chart stays one static view until the core meets its success criteria (INT-67).

items.recommendation: All four kinds: Daniel named each one, a supervisor sent #62 back until variants and dropdowns existed, and the contract is small enough to fix now (TYP-77).

items.title: Playback
items.question: How does a playable chart step through its frames (for example years), and do its marks glide smoothly between frames, which PR #62 does not do?
items.why: Fixes what readers see when a chart animates and what a still, print or PDF shows. S27-648 asked for “sensible frame seeking and restart behavior, a clearly visible current value and smooth transitions with stable mark identity” and to “Handle changing membership, missing values, interrupted playback and reduced motion intentionally”. The branch redraws the whole chart on every change and leaves frame order, restart and missing rows to accident, so most of the rules below are new work.
items.proposed: `kind: playback` steps through the values of one field. Frames are its distinct values, ascending for numbers and dates and in first-appearance order for text; rows without a value for the field belong to no frame. Above the chart sit previous, play/pause and next, a scrubber and the current value, announced to screen readers; ← and → step, and Space plays or pauses. Playback starts only when the reader presses play. Speed defaults to 800 ms per frame and `loop` to true; with `loop: false` playback stops on the last frame, and play then restarts from the first. Changing another control, dragging the scrubber or stepping pauses playback. Line and area charts reveal the series up to the frame; other charts show the frame's rows. Marks keep their identity and glide between real positions; a mark whose row is missing in a frame fades out and returns with its row, and readouts, labels, Table and CSV never show a value between frames. Axes follow FEA-BR-31. The chart opens on the authored `initial` frame, else the last, and PDF export shows that frame and names it; browser print shows the frame on screen and names it (FEA-CH-67). Without JavaScript or WebGL the chart's frame shows ARC-05's notice; no static frame is drawn. Under reduced motion, play advances one frame per press and marks move without gliding.

options.label: Glide between frames
options.detail: What S27-648 asked for (“smooth transitions with stable mark identity”); new work, since the branch redraws the whole chart on every change.

options.label: Step redraw, as on the branch
options.detail: Built for scatter and bar charts and simpler; frames jump, so playback reads as a slideshow, and the branch's redraw fails on line charts.

items.recommendation: Glide between frames: motion is the point of playback, the rule against invented values governs readouts and tables, not the movement between two real frames, and Daniel's INT-12 answer puts motion that explains change and gives pleasure inside the craft.

items.title: Axes during playback
items.question: During playback, do the axes stay fitted to all frames, or refit to each frame as on #62?
items.why: Fixed axes are what make Gapminder-style motion readable: a mark that moves right got richer. On #62 the scatter refits both axes and the size key's reference value on every change, so a mark can move while its value stays put. S27-648 asked that “selectors, playback and whole-chart variants cooperate without stale axes, broken state or duplicate implementations”.
items.proposed: During playback the value axes, the size scale and the colour scale are fitted once to the rows of all frames under the current filter, metric and variant, and do not change between frames. They refit only when another control changes. `axes.*.min` and `max` still pin a range.

options.label: Fit all frames
options.detail: Marks move only when their values change; a frame with small values can sit in a corner of a range fitted to the largest.

options.label: Refit each frame, as on the branch
options.detail: Each frame fills the plot; motion mixes value changes with scale changes, and the size key changes its reference between frames.

items.recommendation: Fit all frames: playback exists to show change, and a moving scale hides it.

items.title: Filter
items.question: Is the filter a one-of choice between listed category values, and does it get an unfiltered option?
items.why: A one-of filter cannot show everything at once: #62's own Gapminder fixture can never show its four regions together. An unfiltered option adds one key to TYP-77.
items.proposed: `kind: filter` restricts the chart's rows to one value of a categorical `field`. The author lists the selectable values in display order in `options`; `all: <label>` adds a first option that shows every row. `initial` picks the starting option, else the first, and exactly one option is active. A category keeps its colour in every state, and axes refit to the selected rows. A selection without rows shows a note instead of an empty plot. An unknown `field` is a `block.field` error. Readouts follow the selection; Table and CSV follow FEA-BR-32. The chart opens on the initial option, and PDF export shows it and names it; without JavaScript or WebGL the frame shows ARC-05's notice.

options.detail: Matches TYP-77 today; showing everything needs a variant.

options.label: Multi-select
options.detail: Most flexible; a checkbox list per chart drifts towards dashboards (INT-33).

items.recommendation: One-of with an “all” option: without it the Gapminder fixture can never show the whole world.

items.title: Metric switch
items.question: Does a metric switch change the measured field together with its whole value axis, using RichView's own format names?
items.why: Fixes how absolute, per-capita or indexed views of one series are offered (FEA-CH-16 routes rebasing here). S27-648 asked for “metric/unit/absolute-versus-relative alternatives with correct labels, scales, values and tooltips”. Keeps d3 format strings out of the format.
items.proposed: `kind: metric` switches the measured field. Each option names its `field` and carries its own value-axis fragment with the T-CHART-AXES fields (`label`, `unit`, `format`, `min`, `max`; TYP-16, TYP-77), so plotted values, ticks, axis title and readouts change together and never drift apart. Tick decimals stay automatic (FEA-CH-23, TYP-86). Formats use the T-VALUE-FORMAT names (TYP-23), never d3 strings. The value axis refits on each switch. Series names, colours and marks stay; only the measure changes. `initial` picks the starting option, else the first; the chart opens on it, and PDF export shows it and names it. Table and CSV follow FEA-BR-32.

items.title: Chart variants
items.question: Can an author give readers named alternative views of one chart (for example bars or a share pie of the same rows), without the composed groups that switch several charts at once, which S27-648 also asked for?
items.why: Variants let one block offer, say, bars and a share-of-total pie of the same data. S27-648 asked for “named variants that replace a whole chart specification or a composed group of charts”; composed groups, swapping several charts together, were never built and would need state shared across charts.
items.proposed: `kind: variant` offers named alternative views. Each option carries a partial chart that replaces the base chart's keys one by one (`type`, `encoding`, `axes`, `data` and so on); `controls` itself cannot be replaced. The base chart and every merged option are validated as charts when the report is checked, so a broken view is an authoring error at its source line, not a broken page; the branch does not do this. The variant applies first; playback, filter and metric then apply to the chosen view. The chart opens on the initial view, and PDF export shows it and names it. Swapping several charts at once (composed groups) is not part of the rewrite. A variant fixture, bars and a share-of-total pie of the same rows, joins the golden inputs (INT-55).

items.title: Control state events
items.question: Are #62's `data-rvc-controls` envelope and its `rv:control` and `rv:control-set` DOM events a public interface of the rewrite, or internal to the runtime?

items.title: Table, downloads, Expand and zoom on charts with controls
items.question: On a chart with controls, do Table and CSV hold every source row, as FEA-CH-45 and FEA-CH-48 say for all charts, or the rows of the state on screen?
items.why: #62's Table and CSV ignore the reader's state: after choosing Asia and 2020 the Table still lists all 64 source rows. FEA-CH-45 calls the Table the chart's non-visual equivalent, which for a filtered chart suggests the rows on screen; FEA-CH-48 makes the CSV the reuse path, where the full set matters. SVG and PNG downloads, Expand, zoom and print need the same answer.
items.proposed: The Table lists the rows of the state on screen and names that state above them (“Asia, 2020: 4 of 64 observations”), with a control to show all rows. The CSV always holds every source row with the fields TYP-36 embeds, as FEA-CH-48 says. SVG and PNG downloads show the chart as on screen and name the state in their title (FEA-CH-46, FEA-CH-47). Expand opens the same state with the same controls, and a change in either view applies to both. Print follows FEA-BR-02. Zoom, readouts and the overview strip (FEA-CH-49, FEA-CH-50) work on the state on screen: a control change keeps the zoom window when it still lies inside the new state's x range, as FEA-CH-71 does for source edits, and otherwise resets it.

items.title: SQL connector (Publish, secondary)
items.question: If RichView's servers serve SQL sources, which safety rules must the connector engine meet, and is PR #66's read-only DuckDB source one option for it?
items.why: Recording the rules now fixes them before any engine is chosen. Daniel's INT-24 answer takes live connectors from an existing third-party engine, and his OPN-63 answer makes them standard on every RichView server. PR #66's branch opens DuckDB read-only, but report SQL can still reach files on the host.
items.proposed: SQL sources are standard on every RichView server, Cowork and Publish, local and hosted, through the connector core RichView builds; PR #66's work enters it (OPN-63, ARC-59). The core never queries data (INT-08): the server loads a report's data through the connector. A block names its SQL source in `.rmd` where it would otherwise name a CSV file: `data.sql` with a connector and a `.sql` file or inline SQL (TYP-79). Whatever engine backs a connector, a SQL source meets these rules: connectors and their credentials live only in the server's configuration, managed by named people, with access granted per person (OPN-63, FEA-SF-19), never in the report, its output, MCP arguments or agent context (ARC-23); queries are read-only, cannot reach host files or networks beyond the declared source, and run with a timeout and a row cap; parameters are bound as values (FEA-BR-43); results carry freshness and provenance (FEA-BR-16). A self-contained HTML file never runs SQL (OPN-63). PR #66's local DuckDB adapter (read-only, only `SELECT` and `WITH`, 100,000-row cap, and `enable_external_access` still to be turned off) is one way to back it; which engines back the connector core, and whether the CLI runs SQL itself or only through a local RichView server, are the agents' technical choice (OPN-63).

items.title: Snapshots, freshness and provenance (Publish, secondary)
items.question: If a RichView server serves stories from live data, do query results travel as snapshots with explicit freshness and a provenance note readers can see?
items.why: Decides how a story that uses live data stays reproducible, and what a reader learns about where the numbers came from and when. Daniel's INT-24 answer keeps exported data the default for every report and makes live data a secondary path, which his OPN-63 answer extends to every RichView server. S27-650 asked for “parameters, result schema/field mapping, useful failures and a cache/refresh contract with explicit freshness”; `ttl`, `freshness` and `refresh` set a cache lifetime, not a refresh schedule (INT-33).
items.proposed: On every RichView server, Cowork and Publish, local and hosted (OPN-63), every connector result is stored by the server as a snapshot, keyed by a SHA-256 fingerprint of connector, query and bound parameters, with a schema giving each field's name, kind (integer, number, string, boolean, date, timestamp or null, as on the branch) and nullability, the row count, capture time and source. A source may set freshness as `ttl` (a duration), `freshness` (a time until which the snapshot stays fresh) or `refresh: true`; a stale snapshot is refreshed by the server or reported as a warning, never used silently. Rendering reads snapshots only, so each published version reproduces from stored data, and a self-contained HTML file carries the data it was rendered from and never queries live data (OPN-63); if TYP-79 keeps `data.cache`, `{key}` reads the snapshot stored under that key. Each chart and table shows a provenance note (connector, query or metrics, capture time) that readers can open.

items.title: Identity, roles and audiences (Publish)
items.question: In the rewrite's Publish, is this the starting access model: identity from an existing provider, #70's three roles (Reader, Editor, Super editor) plus a publishing service identity, audience checks on every route and reports isolated from the desk, to be mapped onto the enterprise-grade roles of FEA-SF-19?
items.why: Access is the security core of Publish, and ARC-57 asks for its rules before any code.
items.proposed:
Built with Publish in the rewrite (INT-31, INT-35, ARC-57), on the server core it shares with RichView Cowork (INT-83):

| Role | Reads | May |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reader | Public items and the audiences granted to them | Nothing editorial |
| Editor | Permitted sections and audiences, with previews | Create drafts, edit source and metadata as pull requests, urgently hide in scope |
| Super editor | Configured scopes | Approve and publish others' changes, curate the site, restore, administer roles |
| Publishing service | Deployment APIs only | Upload, stage and activate approved builds; never an editorial role |

Identity comes from an existing provider (Cloudflare Access on #70) through verified signed tokens; Publish stores no passwords. Every route checks audience and scope, including assets, downloads, previews, search and old releases, and a refused request reveals nothing about the item. Reports run in sandboxed frames that cannot reach the desk's authenticated origin, dashboard SVGs are served as script-free images, and items embed no outside services (FEA-BR-23). The member edition at `/internal` is an authenticated, unindexed view of the same release and never the security boundary; a wholly internal publication is FEA-BR-45.

In the browser these roles act only as Daniel's INT-26 answer allows: a super editor approves or rejects a pending change, and an item's author edits its source (FEA-BR-27). An editor's other rights, such as drafts and edits to items they did not write, are exercised through Git; urgent hide is FEA-BR-28.

Open: how these roles map onto the enterprise-grade roles and governance section the shared server core gives both servers (FEA-SF-19, INT-06). FEA-SF-19 leaves the identity source and single sign-on to the agents, for Cowork and Publish alike.

items.title: Browser editorial desk (Publish)
items.question: In the rewrite's Publish, does its browser desk offer only the two actions Daniel's INT-26 answer allows: approving or rejecting a pending change, and an item's author making a quick source edit in an embedded code editor?
items.why: Daniel asked for a desk in S27-655 (“A small browser editorial surface must make quick source/text/metadata edits, adjustments and hiding practical”), while INT-26 rules out a browser editor for RichView core.
items.proposed:
Publish, built in the rewrite (INT-31, INT-35), has a browser desk that offers two actions and nothing more (INT-26):

- **Approve:** an editor opens a pending change with its protected preview and clicks yes or no on that exact head: a yes on a submission from an author who isn't an editor publishes it publicly, and a yes on the editor's own private item makes it public (FEA-BR-26, OPN-54).
- **Quick source edit:** signed in as an item's author, Edit opens the item's Rich Markdown source at an explicit commit in an embedded VS Code-style code editor with syntax highlighting (library open, ARC-03). Before saving, the server validates and renders the edited report through the core; if either fails, it refuses the save and shows the diagnostics at their source lines. A saved edit becomes an attributed pull request and goes through the same approval.

The desk is never WYSIWYG and keeps no content of its own. It refuses a public repository, detects a publication branch that moved since opening, and keeps unsaved text on conflict. Creating items or drafts, editing `site.yaml` and editing other people's items are not browser actions: they happen in Git through the author's editor and agent. The desk's rules, validation and rendering run in Rust on the server core Publish shares with RichView Cowork, which offers the same two actions (INT-26, INT-83), behind a thin host adapter, such as a Worker adapter if Publish runs on Cloudflare (INT-52, ARC-03; where Publish runs is open in INT-35); the embedded editor is the only browser JavaScript it adds, and #70's JavaScript desk is not carried.

items.title: Immutable releases and rollback (Publish)
items.question: In the rewrite's Publish, are releases immutable and atomically activated, with rollback that keeps current access limits?
items.why: Fixes how a publication changes and recovers. S27-655 asked that “A failed or superseded build must not replace the last good release; an older job finishing late must not overwrite a newer publication”.
items.proposed: Built with Publish in the rewrite (INT-31, INT-35): every build produces an immutable release from pinned source and toolchain, and activation switches one pointer atomically; a stale job is rejected. items.title: Connector checks for the live-data path
items.question: What proves a RichView server's live-data path safe and correct, whichever third-party connector engine is chosen?
items.why: PR #66's adapter could read any host file through SQL (FEA-BR-14), and OPN-63 leaves the engine open. RichView configures the engine, so RichView must own the proof.
items.proposed: RichView keeps a conformance suite that every engine behind its connector core must pass before it is adopted (OPN-63), run against local fixture databases on loopback: writes are refused; queries reach no host file or network beyond the declared source; timeouts and row caps hold; parameters are bound, so injection strings stay values (FEA-BR-43); snapshots are keyed and reused, freshness is honoured and staleness reported, and provenance is visible to readers (FEA-BR-16); credentials never appear in output, logs, diagnostics or agent context (DEL-55's patterns over the rendered output); a person without a grant cannot query a connector (FEA-SF-19); a self-contained HTML file makes no live query, and a URL source fetches only its declared URL (OPN-63); and a published version re-renders from its snapshots with the source offline. Fast safety cases are unit tests that run in the fast gate when a change touches the connector path (DEL-81); the conformance suite runs in the release run for a batch that touches it, and in full at the candidate.
